content: The WHO treatment recommendations for Candida albicans, Trichomonas vaginalis, Mycoplasma genitalium, bacterial vaginosis, and human papillomavirus (anogenital warts) are informed by a systematic review and evidence-to-decision framework. Below are the findings from various studies and reviews: 1. Fluconazole (oral 150 mg single dose) vs. Clotrimazole (intravaginal 10% cream single dose): The short-term microbiological cure rates showed little to no difference between the two treatments. Side effects were also comparable between the two interventions. 2. Fluconazole (oral 150 mg single dose) vs. Clotrimazole (intravaginal 500 mg single dose or multiple doses): A review by Mendling (2020) reported that single-dose clotrimazole had similar cure rates to fluconazole and longer clotrimazole regimens. 3. Fluconazole (oral 150 mg single dose) vs. Miconazole (1200 mg intravaginal capsule x1 or 400 mg intravaginally at night x3): Short-term clinical cure rates were assessed, but the differences were not clinically significant. 4. Fluconazole (oral 150 mg single dose) vs. Miconazole vaginal cream (2%, 5 g intravaginally at night x7): No randomized controlled trials (RCTs) were available for this comparison. 5. Fluconazole (oral 150 mg single dose) vs. Econazole (150 mg intravaginally x1): Short-term clinical cure rates were evaluated, but no significant differences were observed. 6. Fluconazole (oral 150 mg single dose) vs. Econazole (150 mg intravaginally x3 days): No RCTs were available for this comparison. 7. Fluconazole (oral 150 mg single dose, repeated on day 3) vs. Fenticonazole (600 mg single dose or 200 mg intravaginally at night x3): Only one RCT was available, which used 600 mg fenticonazole on days 1 and 3. The results showed no significant differences in outcomes. 8. Fluconazole (oral 150 mg single dose) vs. Itraconazole (200 mg orally twice daily for 1 day): A study by Pitsouni (2008) reported treatment success rates, but there were differences in effects across studies, with high heterogeneity (I² > 50%). 9. Nystatin for recurrent vulvovaginal candidiasis: A Cochrane review (Cooke 2022) included one RCT with 330 women (78% with Candida albicans). It compared oral fluconazole with vaginal suppositories of nystatin (200,000 units per day for 14 days). The fluconazole group had an 8% cure rate (104/141). 10. Nystatin vs. Imidazoles in pregnant women: A Cochrane review (Young 2001) included four RCTs comparing nystatin (100,000 units twice daily for 15 days) with imidazoles. Imidazoles showed higher cure rates (84% vs. 53% for nystatin). 11. Clotrimazole in pregnant women: A review by Mendling (2020) synthesized evidence from five RCTs (1974–1985) and found that clotrimazole (vaginal tablet or cream for 6–7 days) resulted in higher cure rates compared to nystatin or single-dose treatments. 12. Patient preference for oral vs. intravaginal antifungal treatments: A review by Denison (2020) included 12 trials (2206 participants) and reported a preference for oral treatments in 52% to 93% of cases. However, selective reporting was likely. 13. Fluconazole (oral 150 mg single dose) vs. Clotrimazole (intravaginal 200 mg x3 days): The risk of cure in the intervention group was based on the assumed risk in the comparison group, with a small difference in outcomes. 14. Fluconazole (oral 150 mg single dose) vs. Miconazole (1200 mg intravaginal capsule x1 or 400 mg intravaginally at night x3): The risk of cure in the intervention group showed minor differences, with overlapping confidence intervals. 15. Fluconazole (oral 150 mg single dose) vs. Econazole (150 mg intravaginally x1): The intervention group showed a lower risk of cure compared to the comparison group, with overlapping confidence intervals. 16. Fluconazole (oral 150 mg single dose, repeated on day 3) vs. Fenticonazole (600 mg single dose or 200 mg intravaginally at night x3): Only one RCT was available, and the results showed no significant differences in outcomes. 17. Fluconazole (oral 150 mg single dose) vs. Itraconazole (200 mg orally twice daily for 1 day): The intervention group showed a higher risk of cure, but there were differences in effects across studies, with high heterogeneity. 18. Summary of findings: The evidence suggests that fluconazole and clotrimazole are comparable in efficacy for short-term microbiological and clinical cures. Imidazoles generally outperform nystatin in terms of cure rates, particularly in pregnant women. Patient preference leans towards oral treatments, but selective reporting may influence these findings. These findings are based on systematic reviews and meta-analyses, with varying levels of evidence quality and heterogeneity across studies.
